def process(worldcities):
    import pandas as pd

    df = worldcities.copy()

    # Keep only rows explicitly marked as a capital city (primary/admin/minor)
    capitals = df[df['capital'].notna()].copy()

    # Ensure numeric population for ranking; missing populations treated as -1 so they never win
    capitals['population'] = pd.to_numeric(capitals['population'], errors='coerce')
    capitals['lat'] = pd.to_numeric(capitals['lat'], errors='coerce')
    capitals = capitals.dropna(subset=['lat'])

    capitals['popRank'] = capitals['population'].fillna(-1)

    # If a country has multiple capitals, keep the one with the largest population
    # (Tie-break deterministically by lat then city name)
    capitals = capitals.sort_values(['country', 'popRank', 'lat', 'city'], ascending=[True, False, False, True])
    topCapitals = capitals.drop_duplicates(subset=['country'], keep='first')

    avgLat = topCapitals['lat'].mean()
    return pd.DataFrame([{'avg_latitude': avgLat}])

def process(worldcities):
    import pandas as pd

    df = worldcities.copy()

    # Keep only capital cities ("primary" in this dataset denotes national capital)
    df = df[df['capital'].astype('string').str.lower().eq('primary')].copy()

    df['population'] = pd.to_numeric(df['population'], errors='coerce')
    df['lat'] = pd.to_numeric(df['lat'], errors='coerce')

    # If there are multiple primary capitals per country, pick the one with the largest population.
    # (Deterministic tie-breakers: higher lat, then city name.)
    df = df.sort_values(['country', 'population', 'lat', 'city'], ascending=[True, False, False, True])
    top = df.drop_duplicates(subset=['country'], keep='first')

    avg_lat = top['lat'].mean()
    return pd.DataFrame({'avg_latitude': [avg_lat]})

def process(worldcities) -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd

    df = worldcities.copy()
    # National capitals are marked as 'primary' in this dataset
    df = df[df["capital"].astype("string").str.lower() == "primary"].copy()

    df["population"] = pd.to_numeric(df["population"], errors="coerce")

    # If a country has multiple primary capitals, keep the one with the largest population
    df = df.sort_values(
        by=["country", "population", "lat", "city"],
        ascending=[True, False, False, True],
        na_position="last",
    )
    topCapitals = df.drop_duplicates(subset=["country"], keep="first")

    avgLat = topCapitals["lat"].mean()
    return pd.DataFrame([{"avg_latitude": round(float(avgLat), 4)}])
